images.title: Growth between two bars
images.purpose: Show that growth is the later bar with the earlier bar taken away.
images.composition: Two vertical bars side by side with wide space between, and one line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Left: a teal #0072B2 bar 36 units tall labelled 1951: 36 crores. Right: a bar 102 units tall at the same scale, same width, its lower 36 units teal and its upper 66 units reddish purple #CC79A7, labelled 2001: 102 crores. A grey #6B7280 dotted line at the height 36 joins the two bars. Beside the purple part: 66 crores. Below: 102 − 36 = 66 crores. Exactly 2 bars.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
bar heights not in the ratio 36 to 102
images.takeaway: Growth is the later bar take away the earlier bar.
images.description: Two bars, 36 crores in 1951 and 102 crores in 2001, with the top 66 crores highlighted and 102 − 36 = 66.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the part of the 2001 bar that is new.

image_decisions.why: Finding growth by taking one bar from another is a picture idea; two bars show it.
